newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's '97 imports of Russia palladium seen down. [Corrected 10:51 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Japan's '97 imports of Russia palladium seen down. [Corrected 10:51 gmt]

text.p: Japanese imports of palladium from Russia under long-term contracts are expected to fall by 10-15 percent in 1997 compared with this year, local traders said on Thursday.

They said palladium's ongoing substitution with nickel in the electronics industry, which accounts for 66 percent of demand for the metal according to British refiner Johnson Matthey, was the major factor behind the expected fall.

"Japan's palladium demand for use in MLCC, (multi-layer ceramic capacitors) peaked in 1995 and its ongoing substitution with nickel will continue to weigh down the market," a senior bullion house official said.
MLCC is the major end-use for palladium within the electronics sector.

Global sales of palladium by Russian platinum group metals export agency Almazjuvelirexport are expected to reach 4.0 million ounces (124 tonnes) this year, according to a market report from Johnson Matthey. (Corrects to "Global sales..." from "Sales to Japan...")
Japan's cumulative imports of platinum and palladium totalled 52.19 tonnes and 59.08 tonnes respectively in the first nine months of 1996, Finance Ministry data showed.

Almazjuvelirexport usually sends a delegation to Japan for the annual export contract talks in mid-December, but the agency said earlier this week it could delay the visit until January or February due to budget problems.

"The talks could be tough as Japan is likely to ask for a reduction in imports of around 15 percent, while the Russians are short of cash and hope to sell as much palladium as they can," one trader said.
Japanese traders said it was now much more profitable and easier to buy palladium and other platinum group metals in the spot market rather than under long-term contract.

"Importing palladium under long-term contract is less important than it used to be when there was concern about supplies. It is now easier to buy spot because there is plenty of metal around," one trader said.
Another said that the one-month delay in platinum group metal shipments from Russia in July was another reason to reduce the country's dependence on possibly insecure long-term supply contracts.
Despite the expected fall in palladium imports, Japanese traders expect platinum shipments to remain stable next year due mainly to buoyant sales in the platinum jewellery sector.
Some 13 Japanese companies, including major trading houses and three bullion houses, have long-term contracts with Russia to import platinum group metals.
